slices.focus: Missed referral handoff exposed by Tasha's own spreadsheet leads to corrective memo and frozen expansion
slices.summary: A furious family complaint reveals that a referral was lost between hospice discharge documentation and bereavement intake — a gap Tasha's own tracking spreadsheet made visible. Miriam freezes expansion plans and has Tasha draft a corrective memo instead of celebrating early attendance gains. Tasha processes the setback with the agent, developing a four-part memo structure (family impact, failure point, how tracking caught it, corrective steps with owners). The core fix is an 'ownership checkpoint' ensuring no referral is considered complete until one named person confirms active follow-up status. Tasha also plans a weekly unresolved-referrals check and a conversation with Miriam to align on the corrective path.
